transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-06-17
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE); Diego Ramos (Redwood SE); Lina Zhou (FernBay Eng Lead); Marco Chen (FernBay SRE); Asha Rao (FernBay Product)

Summary:
High-level POC scoping to determine workload footprint, success criteria and benchmark plan for FernBay's conversational assistant used in financial onboarding and KYC flows. Customer has spiky QPS during batch account openings, needs cost predictability and strict audit logs.

Topics:
- Current traffic shape and bursts
- Token mix (short prompts + long replies for explanations)
- Concurrency and tail-latency targets
- Benchmarks: replay vs synthetic, success metrics
- Timeline: 4–6 week POC with two benchmark phases

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: alright everyone hi thanks for joining, this is Samira from Redwood, i'm the AE on this, a short intro we'll be mapping the traffic envelope and validating latency/cost tradeoffs for the POC
[00:08] Lina: hey, thanks, i'm Lina, lead on the onboarding assistant. Quick note — we do a lot of form-driven prompts, and then the assistant composes multi-paragraph explanations, so output lengths can vary
[00:17] Diego: hi all, Diego from engineering, i'll own the test harness. quick question — do you have a representative logs export or are we building synthetic traffic
[00:26] Asha: we can do both, but we prefer a log-replay first; we want fidelity to our bursts. typical weekday sustained qps is low, like 10-ish, then we get onboarding pushes that spike briefly
[00:37] Marco: yeah to add to that, peaks have been as high as 380 qps during a batch import, albeit for minutes; sustained peaks are usually 60–80 qps when marketing promos run
[00:46] Samira: okay that's helpful, so let's capture two axes: normal steady-state qps ~10–15, and rare flash bursts to 350–400 for short windows. we'll need token distribution too — what are your average prompt and reply sizes
[00:55] Lina: average user input is pretty short, 8–16 tokens after normalization, replies are larger — mean around 220 tokens but we have a 95th at ~640 tokens when explaining rules
[01:05] Diego: got it, so token mix is skewed. for sizing we'll need concurrency targets — how many concurrent chats per shard do you usually have
[01:12] Marco: concurrent opens during peak roughly 70–90 conversations, but not all request at once — the spike has high instant qps because of parallel step processing
[01:19] Samira: ok so for the POC success criteria proposal: we suggest measuring end-to-end p95 latency under production replay at target qps, and separately stress test to p99 tail under synthetic bursts. any redlines for latency or cost from your side
[01:30] Asha: business wants p95 below 700ms for short replies and p95 below 2s for long generative replies, otherwise user feedback drops. Cost target is a soft target — we want a 20–30% improvement vs our current self-hosted baseline
[01:40] Diego: note, model quality is also gating — we can't sacrifice hallucination and accuracy for cost. can we capture a small eval set to validate quality during bench runs
[01:48] Lina: yes we can provide a 500-sample eval set with labeled expected outputs and a few golden prompts
[01:55] Samira: perfect. for the bench plan i propose three phases: data ingestion and redaction, baseline replay (7 days), and burst stress + tuned routing. timeline about 4–6 weeks: week1 logs + infra, week2 baseline runs, week3 tuning/quantization tests, week4 final validation. can you confirm timeline constraints
[02:12] Asha: OK that maps to our release windows; we'd prefer to finish before the end of july, so that works
[02:18] Marco: small ops note — our environment is VPC with strict egress; we will need an IP allowlist and connector via our transit gateway or a peering setup
[02:26] Diego: we can do both hosted with VPC peering and also show a Dedicated plan in parallel. for the POC we'll run in Redwood hosted but isolated with dedicated tenancy to match perf characteristics
[02:36] Samira: about metrics, we'll capture tokens-per-request, tokens-per-second, GPU utilization, queuing delays, and KV cache hit rate — do you currently use any cache for repeated prompts
[02:45] Lina: we have some caching on templates, but not prefix KV caching. many of the prompts are unique which lowers hit rate
[02:51] Diego: ok, then prefix caching gains may be limited, we'll still measure it. also want to instrument tail latency p99 and p999 if possible since you noted bursts
[02:58] Marco: network egress and TLS termination times i think add ~40–80ms in our stack, that's accounted for in our current SLAs
[03:06] Samira: perfect. for cost modeling we will provide a per-million-token estimate across three model variants — small/fast/cheap, medium, and large/quality — and then show routing policy recommendations
[03:16] Asha: that helps. also SOC2 and audit logs are requirements for production; for POC we need access to security docs and an outline of audit log retention
[03:25] Samira: we'll share our SOC2 summary and security whitepaper, and note retention options; i'll put the doc links in the follow-up
[03:31] Diego: technical detail — what about ephemeral KV cache size and kv eviction policy? our long dialogues sometimes reuse context up to 3–5 previous turns
[03:39] Lina: yes we often include multi-turn context; average context window is 2–3 turns, up to 6 for complex accounts
[03:45] Diego: okay we'll model that in the replay harness. on the benchmarking side, do you want us to run quantized variants to test cost savings or stick to FP16
[03:53] Marco: run both — we want to see degradation curves. but we need quality gating; if quantization increases hallucination beyond threshold it's a no-go
[04:01] Samira: agreed. next, success criteria draft (we'll add to the shared spec):
- Functional: generated replies match golden eval at least 85% for critical flows
- Performance: p95 < 700ms for short replies (<= 150 tokens), p95 < 2s for long replies (>150 tokens) under baseline replay
- Resilience: no more than 1% error rate during 10 minute synthetic bursts at 300 qps
- Cost: demonstrable reduction of at least 20% in token-inferred cost vs current self-hosted during equivalent throughput
[04:27] Asha: that seems reasonable, can we get those as explicit test cases so our compliance team can sign off
[04:33] Samira: yes, we'll put explicit gating tests in the bench doc
[04:36] Diego: instrumentation — we'll attach tracing hooks and per-token timing; please provide a list of event names you log so we can map
[04:42] Lina: we'll send over span names and sample traces; also note some PII must be redacted
[04:48] Samira: perfect, so immediate asks: logs export (7 days), golden eval, VPC config. We'll also need an allowlist for the Redwood side to connect
[04:55] Marco: i'll coordinate the logs and the allowlist but need contact for networking operations
[05:00] Samira: samira.patel@redwood.com — and diego.ramos@redwood.com for SE contact
[05:06] Asha: fine. one more question — if we hit the p95 targets but cost savings are marginal, would Redwood propose hybrid routing (small model for templates, large model for final summary)
[05:16] Diego: yes, we'll model dynamic routing and show expected token-weighted cost. we can also demonstrate semantic rerankers to avoid large outputs when not needed
[05:24] Lina: are there any benchmarks you need from us for model size selection — like latency sensitivity to sequence length
[05:30] Diego: we'll run sequence length sweep tests: 32/128/512/1024 tokens to profile latency per token and memory footprint
[05:36] Samira: ok wrapping up — recap and next steps
[05:39] Samira: we will share the bench spec and a traffic replay template (link included), start infra provisioning, and expect logs by 2029-06-21. target first baseline run week of 2029-06-24
[05:52] Marco: noted — i'll get the logs to you and loop in our netops for allowlist
[05:57] Asha: thanks all
[06:00] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the replay kickoff
